claims.text: A framework coupling molecular dynamics, machine-learning-calibrated interatomic potentials, first-principles data, and thermodynamic modeling can predict melting and liquid-phase behavior in high-entropy alloys.
The framework can predict melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and key liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The proposed framework is computationally efficient across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Machine-learning-calibrated interatomic potentials validated against DFT can capture the essential interatomic forces in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning optimization against first-principles benchmarks produces a sufficiently accurate energy landscape for modeling melting.
Local lattice distortions and short-range ordering evolve during heating.
Local distortions and short-range ordering modulate the thermodynamic barriers to melting.
Accurate representation of the energy landscape enables prediction of latent heat and entropy change at melting.
Accurate representation of the energy landscape enables prediction of volume change at melting.
Knowledge learned from one alloy system can be transferred to other high-entropy-alloy systems.
Transfer across alloy systems can reduce reliance on extensive experimental calibration.
Predictions should agree with high-precision DSC and X-ray measurements to within 5% across a wide high-entropy-alloy composition range.
Traditional calorimetry and CALPHAD-based approaches often require substantial experimental input.
Traditional methods may not generalize efficiently across the large compositional space of high-entropy alloys.
The framework is primarily applicable to high-entropy alloys without extreme chemical ordering or phase separation.
Predictions may be less reliable for alloys containing unconventional bonding environments or unknown complex phases.
